events.description: A public speech by Isabel Schnabel, a member of the ECB's Executive Board. Markets watch these closely for hints about the Governing Council's thinking on future interest rate moves, ahead of the formal policy statement.

A public speech by Pierre Wunsch, a member of the ECB's Governing Council (Governor of the National Bank of Belgium). Lower-profile than a Board speech, but still scanned for any shift in tone on inflation or rates.

A survey measuring how optimistic or pessimistic US consumers feel about the economy, their income, and jobs. Stronger-than-expected confidence tends to support the dollar as it points to healthy consumer spending ahead.

A public speech by Christopher Waller, a member of the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors. His comments are watched for signals on the Fed's next move, particularly this week with the FOMC decision the following day.

A public appearance by Catherine Mann, an external member of the Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee. Mann has historically taken a more hawkish stance, so any change in tone can move sterling.

The Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee (FOMC) announces its target range for the US federal funds rate. This is one of the single biggest drivers of the US dollar and global markets — a surprise move (or surprise language in the statement) can cause sharp swings across all major currency pairs.

The Fed Chair takes questions from reporters straight after the rate decision. Often more market-moving than the decision itself, since this is where the Fed explains its reasoning and gives clues about what comes next.

Japan's headline Consumer Price Index, measuring the change in prices for a typical basket of goods and services. A key input for the Bank of Japan's policy decisions, and released just ahead of this week's BoJ meeting.
An early estimate of quarterly economic growth in Germany, the Eurozone's largest economy. Often moves the euro ahead of the full Eurozone GDP figure released later the same morning.
An early estimate of quarterly economic growth across the whole Eurozone. One of the most closely watched growth indicators for the euro, as it feeds directly into the ECB's outlook for the bloc.
A public speech by Philip Lane, the ECB's Chief Economist. His remarks are watched particularly closely as he's seen as a bellwether for the Governing Council's internal economic thinking.

events.event: Bank of England interest rate decision
events.description: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) announces its decision on the Bank Rate, the UK's main interest rate. This is the single biggest scheduled event for sterling each cycle — a surprise decision or shift in the accompanying vote split can move GBP sharply.

events.event: BoE Monetary Policy Report & Financial Stability Report
events.description: Published alongside the rate decision, this sets out the Bank's updated forecasts for inflation and growth, plus its assessment of risks to the UK financial system. Markets read this for clues on the future path of rates.

The Governor of the Bank of England answers questions from journalists straight after the rate decision. Often the moment that moves sterling most, as it's where the Bank explains its reasoning in its own words.
An early estimate of German inflation, released ahead of the full Eurozone inflation figure. As the bloc's largest economy, Germany's number often sets the tone for how the euro reacts the next day.

The first official estimate of US economic growth for the quarter. A core input into how the Fed and markets judge the health of the world's largest economy — surprises here tend to move the dollar broadly.

The Personal Consumption Expenditures price index — the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation. Often more market-moving than CPI because of how directly it feeds into the Fed's own policy framework.

The number of people filing for unemployment benefits for the first time that week. A high-frequency, early read on the US labour market; usually a minor mover unless it deviates sharply from expectations.

events.event: Bank of Japan interest rate decision
events.description: The Bank of Japan announces its target for short-term interest rates. Following the BoJ's recent shift toward tighter policy, each decision is watched closely for signs of further rate rises, which tend to strengthen the yen.
The BoJ Governor explains the decision and answers questions from the press. Often moves the yen more than the decision itself, particularly any comments on the pace of future policy normalisation.
An early estimate of Eurozone-wide inflation for the month. One of the key inputs into the ECB's interest rate decisions, and a regular source of euro volatility on release.
The percentage of the Eurozone workforce that is unemployed. A slower-moving indicator that rarely surprises markets, but still forms part of the broader picture of Eurozone economic health.
A regional survey of purchasing managers in the Chicago area, used as an early signal for the following week's national ISM manufacturing survey. Usually a modest, secondary market mover.
